svg.title: Method interceptor chain
svg.desc: How every AdviceSource contributes rows to one compiled ProxyPlan, how ProxyClassGenerator emits a single proxy class per bean carrying one interceptor property and one baked descriptor factory per advice kind, and how a call then runs security at advice order 100 before transaction at order 1000 through MethodInvocation::proceed().
svg.text: One proxy per bean: how an advice becomes a link in the chain
packages/data/src/Proxy/{Advice.php, AdviceSource.php, ProxyPlanner.php, ProxyPlanCompiler.php, ProxyClassGenerator.php, ProxyFactory.php, InterceptorRegistry.php, MethodInvocation.php}
packages/security/src/Access/Method/{MethodSecurityAdviceSource.php, MethodSecurityInterceptor.php} · packages/data/src/{Proxy/TransactionalAdviceSource.php, Transaction/TransactionInterceptor.php}
Scan and compile — php artisan firefly:cache (or an in-process scan of firefly.scan.paths when there is no cache)
MethodSecurityAdviceSource
#[Component] in firefly/security
advice(): Advice('security', MethodSecurityInterceptor,
SecurityMethodDescriptor, order 100, inertWhenUnbound: true)
TransactionalAdviceSource
#[Component] in firefly/data
advice(): Advice::transactional() — Advice('tx',
TransactionInterceptor, TransactionalDescriptor, order 1000)
…any other AdviceSource
The port is open: a package contributes a kind of advice
by shipping one #[Component] that implements
AdviceSource — advice(), scan($psr4), render($row).
ProxyPlanner merges every source's scan() rows into one ProxyPlan:
class → method → the ordered (advice id, descriptor row) pairs — sources merge in Advice::order, so each list is outermost-first
ProxyPlanCompiler var_exports the plan into proxy-plan.php — a literal the cached boot requires without reflecting
ProxyClassGenerator writes ONE class per bean: final class Foo__FireflyTransactionalProxy extends Foo
The generated proxy — one member pair PER ADVICE KIND the class uses
private MethodInterceptor $__fireflySecurityInterceptor; · private MethodInterceptor $__fireflyTxInterceptor;
static __fireflySecurityDescriptor('m') / __fireflyTxDescriptor('m') — the descriptors baked as literals, no lookup, no reflection
Runtime — one call, resolved from the container as the proxy, wrapped by ProxyFactory with the interceptors InterceptorRegistry hands it
$accounts->transfer($amount)
the caller holds the proxy, not the bean
(new MethodInvocation($this, AccountService::class, 'transfer', [$amount],
[$this->__fireflySecurityInterceptor, $this->__fireflyTxInterceptor],
[SecurityMethodDescriptor::class => self::__fireflySecurityDescriptor('transfer'), TransactionalDescriptor::class => …],
fn (array $__fireflyArgs) => parent::transfer(...$__fireflyArgs)))->proceed()
order 100
MethodSecurityInterceptor — reads SecurityMethodDescriptor, evaluates #[PreAuthorize] and #[PreFilter],
writes a narrowed argument back with setArguments(), then proceed(). A refusal throws HERE — before any transaction exists.
order 1000
TransactionInterceptor — reads TransactionalDescriptor: propagation, isolation, readOnly, the enforced timeout,
the rollback rules. Opens or joins the transaction through TransactionTemplate::execute(), then proceed().
terminal: parent::transfer(...$args) — the real method, receiving whatever the list holds when it is finally reached
Unwinding, outermost LAST: TransactionInterceptor commits or rolls back, then MethodSecurityInterceptor's after()
applies #[PostAuthorize] and #[PostFilter] to the value the method returned.
Lower advice order runs OUTER — the same ordering Spring documents for @EnableMethodSecurity against @EnableTransactionManagement. It is what makes
"a refusal never opens a transaction" a property of the compiled plan rather than a convention anyone has to remember.
An advice whose interceptor bean is absent is refused at boot (ConfigurationException) unless it declared inertWhenUnbound — security does, because
"annotations are inert until firefly.security.enabled is on" is its documented state — and InterceptorRegistry then hands the proxy a PassThroughInterceptor.
